Name: Introduction to Computer and Systems Sciences

Prerequisites:
Course analysis (HT2025): Course analysis (pdf)
Timetable: Timetable
Aim
According to the course syllabus
Upon successful completion of the course, the student must have knowledge of and be able to explain fundamental concepts in:
- data representation;
- computer architecture;
- operating systems;
- computer networks;
- the Internet;
- data communications;
- algorithms;
- programming;
- software engineering;
- databases;
- computer graphics;
- artificial intelligence;
- theory of computation;
- human–computer interaction;
- computer security.

The student shall also have acquired basic programming skills.

Content
According to the course syllabus
The course is an introduction to the field of Computer and Systems Sciences. Throughout the course, students acquire knowledge of fundamental concepts in areas such as computer architecture, operating systems, computer networks, software engineering, and databases. The course also includes an introduction to programming.

Instruction
According to the course syllabus
Instruction is given in the form of lectures and supervision sessions.

Examination
According to the course syllabus
The course is examined through a written examination and assignments.
All assignments must be performed and submitted on time according to the schedule of the current course offering. A missed or incomplete assignment can be re-submitted at a newly scheduled time window. Alternatively, the student will have to follow the schedule of the next course offering.

Literature

    ISBN: 978-0-13-487546-0
